text:
anna: quick heads-up from today's perf run — seeing p95/p99 tail jumps under sustained qps for long-seq requests. dug into kernel selection + kv behavior.

mike: paste the numbers you saw?

anna: microbatch=16, seq_len=2048, model=redwood-13b-ql4, gpu_util=88% (sustained), p95=420ms, p99=980ms, kv_hit=0.67, kv_miss_cost ~= +180ms. profiler shows many requests falling back to cu_attention for the final chunks (triton_fused_attn handles steady-state but tripped on some sequence patterns).

julia: interesting — so not a pure batching issue, looks like a kernel mismatch on tails that only appears when util is high.

chetan: that's classic saturation: high avg util hides tail cost of fallback kernels. if we target lower util we buy headroom for those fallbacks.

mike: proposal A: lower target_gpu_util from 85% -> 70% for this workload class, keep microbatch ceiling at 32 but set microbatch floor to 8 when latency SLOs tighten. admission kicks in once queue_length > 4 * num_gpus.

anna: tested something similar on canary: new admission rule + microbatch floor=8 reduced p95 by ~22% and p99 by ~45% at same throughput, throughput dropped ~9%.

julia: 9% throughput loss for 45% p99 improvement seems reasonable for user-facing low-latency routes.

mike: alternative B: smarter kernel routing — detect tail sequences and force triton_fused_attn path earlier (or recompile kernels to handle those edge patterns). longer-term but lower throughput impact.

anna: recompile path will take cycles; meanwhile we can tune kvcache: prefetch window=4 reduced p95 by 18% in tests (cost: ~3% extra GPU memory and slight variance). when kv_hit < 0.5 we should be more conservative on batching.

chetan: load-shedding idea: drop or deprioritize low-value queries (embeds/metrics) during high-saturation windows; or convert them to best-effort. shed budget = oldest low-priority until queue_size <= threshold.

sre-oncall: flag — we need deterministic SLO rules that are easy to audit. can we sum this into a small set of pluggable knobs? e.g. {target_util, microbatch_floor, admission_threshold, kvcache_prefetch, shed_policy}

anna: agreed. actionables:
- anna: open RFC with canary results + config defaults (will include the perf output and kernel traces)
- mike: implement simple admission policy config + microbatch floor toggle in runtime (canary in 3 nodes)
- julia: start a kernel triage ticket with model team (investigate fused kernel correctness on tails)
- chetan: prototype shed policy for low-priority queues

infra-bot: perf-canary job 51234 completed — artifacts: https://internal.redwood/perf/51234 (contains profiler flamegraphs, kernel selection traces, kvcache stats)

mike: quick note on thresholds: from canary I'd recommend default target_util=72%, microbatch_floor=8, admission_queue_threshold=6, kvcache_prefetch=4, shed=enabled for priority="best-effort".

julia: +1 to defaults. we'll document SLO impacts and rollback path in the RFC.

sre-oncall: please schedule the canary during low-cost window and set automated rollback if p99 > previous by 10% for 10m.

anna: will do. i'll also attach minimal repro (run_perf snippet) to the RFC so infra can reproduce locally:

```
# repro snippet
run_perf --model redwood-13b-ql4 --seq 2048 --microbatch 16 --qps 80 --warmup 2000 --log-kernels
```

mike: thanks — nice, pragmatic plan. i'll start the runtime patch and land a feature-flag behind `runtime.dynamic_admission_v2`.

anna: :thumbsup: will follow up with RFC link in this thread. recommend we avoid aggressive global util increases until kernel fixes land.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary roll queued for 3 nodes, feature-flag=off initially.
